title: NY State Assembly · District 39
area: Corona, Elmhurst, Jackson Heights and parts of Middle Village and Rego Park, Queens.

context.text: Incumbent Catalina Cruz defeated Yonel Letellier Sosa 90.9%-8.1% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Letellier Sosa's attempt to also appear in November on the Affordable & Safe Party line was withdrawn or disqualified, so he is not on the general-election ballot. Ramses Frias advanced from the Republican primary without opposition; a separate attempt to also place Frias on the Conservative Party line was withdrawn or disqualified, so he appears only on the Republican and 4 Our Immigrants Party lines.

priorities.text: Describes her legislative focus as immigrant rights, tenant protections and workers' rights, citing her background as a formerly undocumented tenant attorney raised by a single working mother.

Her official biography states she has "passed more than 20 new laws to combat food insecurity, curtail the high cost of healthcare, protect aging New Yorkers and so much more" since taking office in 2019.
priorities.quote: Since taking office in 2019, Catalina has passed more than 20 new laws to combat food insecurity, curtail the high cost of healthcare, protect aging New Yorkers and so much more.

positions.summary: Cosponsored A1466, the New York Health Act (2025–26 session), which would create a universal single-payer health plan (New York Health) for state residents.

In an August 2021 press release, called on the governor to sign the remaining gun-violence bills the Legislature had passed, including A.2666-A on unfinished firearm frames and receivers and A.613 on serial numbers for "ghost guns".

record.text: Serves on the Codes, Ethics and Guidance, Health, Insurance, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored A00270, establishing a right to legal counsel in immigration court proceedings; referred to the Codes Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A00176 (print no. A00176A), allowing state agencies, municipalities and authorities to provide public benefits regardless of immigration status; amended and recommitted to the Social Services Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A10021, which would bar denying children access to free public education based on their own or their parents' actual or perceived citizenship or immigration status; referred to the Education Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A08516, authorizing the DMV to issue standard driver's licenses while restricting what applicant information can be retained or disclosed; referred to the Transportation Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A00352, authorizing the state to withhold Medicaid reimbursements from retail entities that refuse to dispense federally approved pregnancy-prevention products; referred to the Health Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

candidates.name: Ramses Frias

priorities.text: His campaign site lists his priorities as restoring quality of life for residents and businesses, educating the community for growth, building a safer future, uniting communities, instilling community pride, amplifying residents' voices, and driving small-business engagement to boost economic growth.

candidates.researchNotes: Frias has not held elected office and has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey. His campaign site lists general goals and an "In the Media" list of Fox News, New York Post and other appearances, but the text of those appearances was not loaded, so no quotes or positions on the guide's issues are recorded.

sources.title: Queens Lawmaker Condemns Rising Gun Violence in Borough and Throughout New York City
